Commentary.Commentary: We are back for the chase! The umpires are back out in the middle and so are the players of Bangladesh. It will be the Indian skipper Rohit Sharma who will open the batting alongside Shubman Gill for India. Taskin Ahmed will get proceedings underway with the ball. Let's go...
... The Run Chase ...

There have been 55 instances of an Indian bowler taking a 5-wicket haul in ODIs - the team has lost only 6 times. The last time India lost when its bowler took a 5-fer was way back in 2019 when Shami's 5/69 went in vain against England in Birmingham. This is the 10th occasion since that date, that an Indian bowler has taken a Michelle, with all the previous 9 resulting in wins. So, are these 228 runs enough on this pitch? This surface is a fresh one but slower too and with not much dew expected, there could be some lateral movement under lights. The batters will have to apply themselves, thus this chase is going to be very exciting. Don’t go anywhere as the action of the second inning isn’t far away.

For India, Mohammad Shami picked up a five-wicket haul and bowled brilliantly as he completed his full quota of overs for the first time in his comeback in ODI after the World Cup 2023. Axar and Harshit also chipped in with two and three wickets respectively to give their contribution. Also, on the last 3 occasions that a player from Bangladesh has scored a century in an ODI, it has resulted in a loss for the team twice. However, the last time it happened was when Najmul Hossain Shanto scored 122 against Sri Lanka in Chattogram in 2024 which means, there is plenty of hope for Bangladesh.

Axar Patel is down for a quick chat. He starts by addressing the hat-trick ball and says that he immediately went on to celebrate when he saw the edge but was gutted when the catch got put down and adds that these things happen. Reckons that yes, if they got that wicket, the innings could have ended sooner but the track did get better for batting. Mentions that the wicket is quite slow and it might get even slower in the chase. Adds that his role is whatever the team need him to do, whether be it with the bat or the ball.

Hridoy and Jaker batted for more than 34 overs, both reaching their half-centuries and setting the record for the highest sixth-wicket partnership in Champions Trophy history. Once they got set, they started accelerating, playing more attacking shots. Eventually, Shami broke the partnership by dismissing Jaker Ali, and in the process, he became the joint-second fastest bowler in terms of matches to take 200 ODI wickets. But by then, Bangladesh had already built a strong platform for the lower order to go for big hits in the death overs and push the total closer to 240. Tawhid Hridoy struggled with his fitness and had to take multiple breaks for physio treatment, but his determination kept him going. He battled through the pain and scored a hard-earned century, ensuring Bangladesh got a good finish. Since he couldn’t run comfortably, he relied more on boundaries in the final overs, playing smartly with the tailenders to get his team to a competitive total.

Rohit Sharma’s decision to bring spin into the powerplay worked perfectly, as Axar Patel struck twice in consecutive deliveries, both caught behind by KL Rahul. He almost got a hat-trick, but Rohit himself dropped a catch at first slip off Jaker Ali’s edge. The Indian skipper looked frustrated with that missed opportunity. Then came the defining partnership of the innings, 154 runs between Tawhid Hridoy and Jaker Ali. They handled the spin trio of Jadeja, Kuldeep, and Axar brilliantly, focusing on rotating the strike rather than taking unnecessary risks. Early on, they scored at just over three runs per over, keeping the scoreboard ticking with singles and the occasional boundary. Hridoy got a lifeline when Hardik Pandya dropped a catch while he was on 23. India’s fielding was sharp overall on the field, but they dropped two straightforward catches and even missed a stumping chance, allowing Bangladesh to recover from their disastrous start.

Mohammad Shami set the tone right from the first over, bowling five dot balls before dismissing Soumya Sarkar on the last delivery. In the very next over, Harshit Rana proved too tricky and raw for Bangladesh’s skipper Najmul Hossain Shanto, who went for an ambitious drive but ended up giving a simple catch to Virat Kohli at cover. As the captain, Shanto should have taken more responsibility and spent some time at the crease, especially after an early wicket, but he failed to do so. Tanzid Hasan tried to counterattack with a couple of boundaries down the ground, but his stay didn’t last long. Mehidy Hasan Miraz was promoted to number four ahead of the experienced Mushfiqur Rahim, but he struggled throughout his short 10-ball stay. His footwork was all over the place, and eventually, Shami tempted him into playing a loose drive, leading to a sharp catch by Shubman Gill at first slip.

That is a good comeback by Bangladesh as they have posted a total of 228! All the credit goes to just two batters, Jaker Ali and Tawhid Hridoy. When Bangladesh lost five wickets for just 35 runs, they were on the verge of getting bowled out without playing the full 50 overs. But these two showed incredible patience and determination at the crease, helping their team cross the 200-run mark. Early in the powerplay, Bangladesh’s batting was terrible, as none of the top six, except Hridoy, tried to settle in and build an innings. Their batting lacked focus, technique, and application, which will surely disappoint them. They were completely outplayed by India’s bowlers, who smartly adjusted their lengths, varied their pace, and extracted turns from the pitch.

Shami goes in from short fine leg and takes the catch, marking the end of a gem of a knock from Hridoy. He gets out on exactly 100 runs and Bangladesh end with 228 runs on the board!

Commentary.Commentary: Had to really hurry there! Full and on middle, Tanzid Hasan clips it in front of mid on and straightaway rushes though for a single. Kuldeep Yadav from mid on runs forward, bends low but fails to collect the ball in a go and the batters complete the single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.4: Harshit Rana to Tanzid Hasan, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Slows the pace down now, does Rana, full around off, Tanzid Hasan waits for it to come and blocks it under his eyes.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.3: Harshit Rana to Tanzid Hasan, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Oh, dragged on nearly! Hard length, on off, Tanzid Hasan stands tall and tries to pull it across but ends up inside edging it onto the boot, and the ball keeps rolling on the strip.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.2: Harshit Rana to Tanzid Hasan, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Two slips in for the left-hander! Rana bashes the hard length, around off, nips away with the angle. Tanzid Hasan feels for it at first, but keeps his bat away from the ball.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.1: Harshit Rana to Tanzid Hasan, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Good early call! Two fours and then a single! Back of a length, angling in on middle, Tanzid Hasan tucks it across and in front of mid on for a quick single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.6: Mohammad Shami to Tanzid Hasan, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! Now that's some shot! Lands it full, does Shami around off, Tanzid Hasan shimmies down the track, opens the bat face, and drives it crisply though covers for a cracking boundary.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.5: Mohammad Shami to Tanzid Hasan, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! Struck well! The first boundary for Bangladesh! Seam-up delivery, well outside off, on a length, Tanzid Hasan gets the chance to free his arms, goes after it in a flash. Clears the in-field over cover-point and gets a boundary.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.4: Mohammad Shami to Tanzid Hasan, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: Swing and a miss! Shami keeps it outside off on a yard behind fuller length. Tanzid Hasan leans back to execute the square cut, but misses.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.3: Mohammad Shami to Tanzid Hasan, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Pitched fuller around off, Tanzid Hasan leans on it and works it to cover-point.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.2: Mohammad Shami to Tanzid Hasan, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Length, on the stumps, knocked across to mid-wicket.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.1: Mohammad Shami to Tanzid Hasan, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: A sharp steep bumper from Rana now. On the bodyline. Mehidy Hasan Miraz tries to opt out but the ball gets big on him and lobs off the glove. Lands behind the stumps in front of the slip cordons.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.6: Harshit Rana to Mehidy Hasan Miraz, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Good length, angling on the pads, Mehidy Hasan Miraz looks to nudge it across but wears it high on the thigh pad.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.5: Harshit Rana to Mehidy Hasan Miraz, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Mehidy Hasan Miraz walks in with Bangladesh in early trouble.

OUT! TAKEN! A fantastic start for India as Harshit Rana too, strikes in his very first over! The lean patch for skipper Najmul Hossain Shanto with the bat continues! Harshit Rana fires it in, from over the stumps. The length is fuller and around off with the ball skidding through quickly off the surface. Najmul Hossain Shanto prods forward to access the cover drive but ends up mistiming it badly. It goes off from a bit of the toe-end of the blade and flat towards Virat Kohli at cover who takes a sharp catch around the chest level. A silver duck for Shanto and Bangladesh are pegged back to 2/2.
Commentary.Howout: c Virat Kohli b Harshit Rana
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.4: Harshit Rana to Najmul Hossain Shanto, OUT! c Virat Kohli b Harshit Rana.

Commentary.Commentary: This one leaves the batter from around off, full in length. Najmul Hossain Shanto shoulders arms at it.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.3: Harshit Rana to Najmul Hossain Shanto, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Hard length, outside off, Tanzid Hasan leans back and cuts it to deep backward point for a single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.2: Harshit Rana to Tanzid Hasan, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Back of a length and outside off, Tanzid hangs back and knocks it to covers.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.1: Harshit Rana to Tanzid Hasan, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Najmul Hossain Shanto, the skipper walks in at number 3. Also, it will be Harshit Rana to take the other new ball.

OUT! CAUGHT BEHIND! Shami with an instant impact as he strikes in the very first over. Bangladesh lose Soumya Sarkar on a five-ball duck! With a perfect seam position, Shami lands it on a good length, outside off. It lands, skids through, and nips back into the left-hander. Soumya Sarkar is half-forward to play it on the off side, but ends up playing it away from the body with his feet not up to the pitch of the ball. Hence, an inside edge is found and a simple catch for KL Rahul behind the pegs.
Commentary.Howout: c KL Rahul b Mohammad Shami

Commentary.Commentary: Hits the deck hard, does Shami. Around off, this is tapped off the back foot to the off side by Soumya Sarkar.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.5: Mohammad Shami to Soumya Sarkar, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Moves a tad closer to the stumps, but still slightly outside off on a hard length. Sarkar offers no shot. The ball nips in a bit and passes above the off pole.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.4: Mohammad Shami to Soumya Sarkar, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Identical line and length, but this goes straight on from outside off, Soumya Sarkar opts to leave it.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.3: Mohammad Shami to Soumya Sarkar, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: BEATEN! Back of a length, with a hint of an away shape from off, Soumya Sarkar flays at it but the ball beats the bat on the way to the keeper.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.2: Mohammad Shami to Soumya Sarkar, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: First runs on the board for Bangladesh, in a streaky manner though! Shami begins with a slip in place, runs in hard from around the stumps, lands it on a length, angling on off. Tanzid Hasan tries to play it off the back foot but inside edges past the stumps to the widish short fine region for a single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.1: Mohammad Shami to Tanzid Hasan, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Done and dusted with the pre-match proceedings and it is now time to play! The Indian players can be seen in a huddle before striding onto the field and the two umpires have taken their places as well. It will be the pairing of Soumya Sarkar and Tanzid Hasan to open the innings for Bangladesh. Mohammad Shami has the new ball in hand and is raring to go. Just a slip in place to begin with, let's go...

We are just a few minutes away from the start of this contest. But first, the officials will come out to the middle and so will the two sets of players who will line up for their respective national anthems. It will be the national anthem of India first, followed by the national anthem of Bangladesh.

The captain of India, Rohit Sharma says that they would have fielded first as he feels that when they played here a few years back, it was better to chase the target. Adds that they now just need to focus on what to do with the ball and says that the squad is fit and ready to go and it is about creating some momentum. Mentions that the case with any ICC tournament is that there's no looking back and every game matters which makes it exciting. Informs that from the last ODI they played, Varun Chakaravarthy misses out and Ravindra Jadeja comes back in and Arshdeep Singh also misses out as Mohammad Shami comes in.

The captain of Bangladesh, Najmul Hossain Shanto says that it looks like a good wicket and they want to put some runs on the board. Adds that the last couple of days have been really exciting as all the boys in the squad are really preparing well and they are coming off recently concluded BPL so they are in good momentum. Mentions that he just wants to play well today and the team should believe in themselves to do good. Further adds that there are a couple of injuries as Tawhid Hridoy has come back. Informs that they are going with three seamers with two spinners.
India (Playing XI) - Rohit Sharma (C), Shubman Gill, Virat Kohli, Shreyas Iyer, Axar Patel, KL Rahul (WK), Hardik Pandya, Ravindra Jadeja, Harshit Rana, Mohammad Shami, Kuldeep Yadav.

Bangladesh (Playing XI) - Tanzid Hasan, Soumya Sarkar, Najmul Hossain Shanto (C), Tawhid Hridoy, Mushfiqur Rahim (WK), Mehidy Hasan Miraz, Jaker Ali, Rishad Hossain, Tanzim Hasan Sakib, Taskin Ahmed, Mustafizur Rahman.
TOSS UPDATE - The coin flip lands in the favor of Bangladesh and Najmul Hossain Shanto elects to BAT first.

PITCH REPORT - Mel Jones is pitchside. She says that the straight boundary is long at 82 meters and there is a 12-meter difference in both squares of the wicket. Says that there have been a couple of tournaments on this ground including the Women's T20 World Cup and the recently concluded ILT20. Nasser Hussain joins her as he says, the pitch does look fresh and there is a bit of crack but it might get a bit tired in 100 overs of play. Mentions that the other thing is dew as he spoke to the groundsmen and they said, there is no dew at all during this season. Reckons that the scores here in Dubai will be lower than those of Pakistan. They both emphasize that the skipper should bat first if they are winning the toss.

The big question now. Will teams lean more on spin or pace? Both India and Bangladesh boast deadly spin attacks capable of dismantling any batting lineup, yet they also pack a punch with their seamers. However, with the natural slowness of the Dubai wicket, we might see spin dictating terms. And with both subcontinental giants well aware and adapted to slow tracks, it makes the contest even more spicier. But how will the pitch play? Stay tuned for the pitch report, the toss, and team updates to see how the captains choose to tackle these tricky conditions.

Shifting the focus to the conditions, Dubai hasn’t seen an ODI between full-member nations since June 2019, and the history of the venue speaks volumes. Run-scoring has never been a walk in the park, with just two 300+ totals in the past. To put it into perspective, the average first-innings score stands at just a tinge above 200. The last encounter between these two sides in this competition took place in the 2017 Champions Trophy semifinal, which remains Bangladesh's best performance in the tournament. India came out on top that day, and they also lead the head-to-head record 7-3 in the last ten ODIs. However, Bangladesh can draw motivation from their 2022 ODI series win over India, a reminder that turnarounds are possible when the right momentum is built.

However, a promising crop of young talent, fueled by impressive performances in the Bangladesh Premier League, offers hope. The absence of stalwarts like Shakib Al Hasan and Litton Das presents a challenge, but veterans Mushfiqur Rahim and Mahmudullah remain key figures and the backbone of the batting unit, with Mehidy Hasan Miraz providing vital all-round strength. Perhaps the most promising aspect of Bangladesh’s setup is their pace bowling. With Taskin Ahmed and Mustafizur Rahman leading the charge, they’re supported by promising young talents like Tanzim Hasan Sakib and the raw pace of Nahid Rana, who turned heads in the recent series against Pakistan. It’s a squad in transition, but one with enough firepower to make an impact.

On the other hand, Bangladesh enters the Champions Trophy eager to recalibrate after a challenging 2024, where they won just three out of nine ODIs and suffered a demoralizing clean sweep against the West Indies. Their goal isn't just to improve their meager record in the tournament, having secured only two wins across all their appearances, but also to rediscover the fearless spirit that once propelled them into the global spotlight. With a point to prove, they’re determined to revive the form that earned them respect on the world stage.

The gears of India's batting machinery are clicking into perfect rhythm at just the right time. Rohit Sharma's return to form, marked by a spectacular century at home, has injected fresh confidence into the top order. The skipper's rediscovered touch couldn't have come at a better moment. Also, the focus remains on Virat Kohli, off a recent fifty, whose uncanny ability to perform under pressure has made him the big-tournament specialist over the years. Kohli’s bat tends to morph into a magic wand during ICC events, and once again, India will count on their stalwarts to lead from the front. However, the team has scored a barrage of 300+ runs for fun in recent years, the form of these two men will only make it challenging for any opposition.

Pooled in Group A, India’s last ICC title success in the ODI format dates back to the 2013 Champions Trophy, as this Indian side arrives in Dubai with renewed vigor and a point to prove. With a perfect blend of experience and emerging talent rounding up their 15-man squad, they're ready to turn the tide in the desert sands. While questions hovered over India's bowling arsenal in Jasprit Bumrah's absence, the recently concluded series against England at home provided emphatic answers with Arshdeep Singh breaking through the opposition batting lineup and Mohammed Shami who fills in for Bumrah. Complementing these seamers is a spin department that is a formidable force - Varun Chakravarthy's mystery paired with Kuldeep Yadav's crafty left-arm wrist spin presents a dual threat. The team’s clinical clean sweep showcased a bowling unit that has evolved beyond dependency on individual brilliance.

Hello, everyone! The ICC Champions Trophy of 2025 has kicked off with a bang. With the curtain raiser setting the tone for what is to follow for the tournament, the competition progresses into Match number 2. We are here at the land of Emirates for the Asian derby as India takes on Bangladesh at the luxurious Dubai International Stadium. On that note, we extend our warm welcome to everyone joining us for the coverage of this spicy rivalry.
... MATCH DAY ...

The wait is over and after a hiatus of 8 years, the ICC Champions Trophy returns! The much-awaited tournament will be played across Pakistan and Dubai with hosts and reigning champions Pakistan looking to repeat their success from 2017. It is now time for Match 2 of the competition between Bangladesh and last time's runners-up India which will be played at the Dubai International Cricket Stadium. While history heavily favors India, Bangladesh's recent cricketing revolution makes them a far cry from the pushovers of yesteryear. This promises to be a captivating encounter, a true test of both teams' mettle. India's batting lineup, a constellation of stars like Virat Kohli, Rohit Sharma, and others, possesses the kind of firepower that can dismantle any bowling attack on its day. Their ability to accelerate and chase down big totals is well-documented. However, they'll be wary of a Bangladeshi bowling unit that has shown it can be dangerous. Mustafizur Rahman's variations and cutters will be a constant threat, and the likes of Taskin Ahmed and Mehidy Hasan Miraz will look to contribute crucial breakthroughs. The last time both teams played an ODI at this venue was back in September 2018 and it was the Asia Cup Final which India won against Bangladesh. India boasts a record of 5 wins in 6 ODI games at this venue which all took place in that 2018 Asia Cup whereas Bangladesh have played 3 and won 1. Talking a bit more about the teams, the biggest miss from India will be Jasprit Bumrah who is out injured and for Bangladesh, their premier all-rounder Shakib al Hasan isn't a part of the squad after failing tests for a suspected bowling action a while back. With the conditions generally pace-friendly in Dubai, India have surprisingly gone with just 3 out-and-out pacers along with Hardik Pandya but they do have 5 proper spinners in the squad which means they want to stick to their strengths regardless of the conditions. On the flip side, Bangladesh have their regular pacers like Taskin Ahmed and Mustafizur Rahman to go along with the likes of Nahid Rana who is an upcoming star for Bangladesh. As for the batting department, that has always been an area of concern whenever Bangladesh play in big tournaments and against the top teams. A lot will ride on skipper Najmul Hossain Shanto at the number 3 position as he would be looking to anchor the innings, allowing the likes of Tawhid Hridoy and Mahmudullah to attack later on. India on the other hand are coming off a fine batting performance in the home series against England and the likes of Rohit Sharma and Virat Kohli were able to find some crucial form with the likes of Shubman Gill and Shreyas Iyer really coming into their own. All in all, the conditions should balance things out a bit, allowing Bangladesh a chance to attack with their seamers but the real challenge will be for their batters against the seasoned and in-form Indian bowling lineup. Also, if the pitch is on the drier side, we might even see some purchase for the spinners in the first innings which could play a huge role as well in this game. Can Bangladesh pull off a huge upset and start their campaign with a bang? Or will India yet again get the better of their neighbors and march on their merry way? Only time will tell.
